scenes.visual: Title card 'Random Moves, One-Way Drift' over a glass of still water with one purple drop just landing. COLOUR MAP (both films): membrane = WHITE DASHED vertical line on a dark navy background; dye = small PURPLE dots; water = small BLUE dots; salt = small GREY squares; oxygen = small GREEN dots; carbon dioxide = small RED dots. Crossing tallies = WHITE arrows with counters above the membrane, '→ N' for left to right and '← N' for right to left. Every tank and cell is a cartoon labelled 'schematic'. Numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: Every dye particle in this glass moves at random. None of them has a direction. So why does a drop of colour always spread out, and almost never gather back into a drop?
scenes.visual: Live-style cartoon: a purple drop lands in a glass of water and slowly blooms outward until the glass is evenly pale purple. A reversed clip tries to pull the colour back into a drop; a red X stamps over it. Question card: 'why only one way?'
scenes.narration: Every dye particle in this glass moves at random. None of them has a direction. So why does a drop of colour always spread out, and almost never gather back into a drop?

scenes.tts: Let's zoom in and build a model. Picture a tank split down the middle by an open line. Most of the purple dots start on the left. Only a few start on the right.
scenes.visual: Camera zooms into the glass and the scene becomes a flat rectangular tank, labelled 'schematic', split by a dotted grey open line. 12 purple dots jiggle on the left, 2 on the right. On-screen counters at the top: 'left: 12' and 'right: 2'.
scenes.narration: Let's zoom in and build a model. Picture a tank split down the middle by an open line. Most of the purple dots start on the left. Only a few start on the right.

scenes.tts: Each dot jiggles along its own path. Any dot that reaches the line may hop across, either way. No dot knows where the crowd is. And nothing pushes any of them.
scenes.visual: Each dot jiggles in its own random path. Now and then a dot that reaches the line flashes white and hops across, sometimes left to right, sometimes right to left. A caption: 'any dot at the line can hop, either way'. No arrows push the dots.
scenes.narration: Each dot jiggles along its own path. Any dot that reaches the line may hop across, either way. No dot knows where the crowd is. And nothing pushes any of them.

scenes.tts: So over many seconds, which way will more dots cross on average? From left to right, or from right to left? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: The tank freezes. Pause card in the centre: 'Over many seconds, which way will MORE dots cross on average?' with two buttons '→' and '←'. A 5-second ring timer appears.
scenes.narration: So over many seconds, which way will more dots cross on average? From left to right, or from right to left? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: Pause card holds; ring timer runs down.

scenes.tts: On average, more cross from left to right. No dot chose that. There are simply more dots on the left to make the hop. A few still hop back. In a short count, luck can make a tie, or even tip it the other way.
scenes.visual: Motion resumes. The tally arrows fire: '→ 3' and '← 1'. The left crowd is highlighted, showing more dots available to hop. One dot hops back from the right, lighting the '←' counter. Counters update to 'left: 10' and 'right: 4'. Small caption: 'on average'.
scenes.narration: On average, more cross from left to right. No dot chose that. There are simply more dots on the left to make the hop. A few still hop back. In a short count, luck can make a tie, or even tip it the other way.

scenes.tts: How crowded a substance is in a space has a name. Concentration is how much of a substance is in a given space. At the start, the left side is more concentrated.
scenes.visual: The word 'concentration' writes on screen with the definition 'how much of a substance is in a given space'. A purple shading bar under each half: dark under the left, pale under the right, labelled 'more concentrated' and 'less concentrated'.
scenes.narration: How crowded a substance is in a space has a name. Concentration is how much of a substance is in a given space. At the start, the left side is more concentrated.

scenes.tts: Keep the hops running. The crowd thins on the left and grows on the right. This drift, from more concentrated to less concentrated, is called diffusion.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse: counters tick on from 10:4 to 8:6 to 7:7 (always 14 dots in all). A thick purple arrow labelled 'diffusion: more concentrated → less concentrated' sweeps left to right under the tank, fading as the shading bars even out.
scenes.narration: Keep the hops running. The crowd thins on the left and grows on the right. This drift, from more concentrated to less concentrated, is called diffusion.

scenes.tts: Now the two sides are about even. Dots still cross, and over time just as many go each way. The colour stops changing, yet the dots never stop moving.
scenes.visual: Counters wobble around even: 'left: 7, right: 7', then '8 : 6', then '7 : 7'. Each counter change matches its short tally window: from 7:7 the arrows fire '→ 2', '← 3' and the counters read '8 : 6'; then '→ 3', '← 2' and the counters return to '7 : 7' (always 14 dots in all). Dots keep jiggling. The shading bars stay about equal. Caption: 'still moving, no change overall'.
scenes.narration: Now the two sides are about even. Dots still cross, and over time just as many go each way. The colour stops changing, yet the dots never stop moving.

scenes.tts: Now swap the open line for a cell membrane. On one side is the blood, crowded with oxygen. Inside a muscle cell, there is much less of it.
scenes.visual: The dotted line morphs into the WHITE DASHED membrane, and the right half becomes a pink cartoon muscle cell, labelled 'schematic'. Left half labelled 'blood' holds many GREEN oxygen dots; the cell holds few.
scenes.narration: Now swap the open line for a cell membrane. On one side is the blood, crowded with oxygen. Inside a muscle cell, there is much less of it.

scenes.tts: The same random hops carry more oxygen into the cell than out of it. Carbon dioxide is more crowded inside the cell, so it drifts out, the other way.
scenes.visual: Tally arrows return for GREEN dots: more '→' than '←'. Then RED carbon dioxide dots crowd inside the cell, and their tally arrows show more crossing from the cell out to the blood. Labels 'oxygen' and 'carbon dioxide'.
scenes.narration: The same random hops carry more oxygen into the cell than out of it. Carbon dioxide is more crowded inside the cell, so it drifts out, the other way.

scenes.tts: The cell spent no energy on any of this. Movement across a cell membrane that needs no energy from the cell is called passive transport.
scenes.visual: A battery icon on the cell stays full with a label 'no energy spent'. The words 'passive transport' write on screen with 'needs no energy from the cell'.
scenes.narration: The cell spent no energy on any of this. Movement across a cell membrane that needs no energy from the cell is called passive transport.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule. Particles move at random, so on average more leave a crowded side than come back. That makes a one-way drift, with no push needed.
scenes.visual: Split screen: on the left the dye tank's tally '→ 3, ← 1'; on the right the membrane with oxygen '→' outnumbering '←'. One shared thick arrow under both: 'crowded → less crowded'.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule. Particles move at random, so on average more leave a crowded side than come back. That makes a one-way drift, with no push needed.

scenes.tts: But what if the crowded particle is one the membrane will not let through? And what if water is the only thing that can cross? That is the next film.
scenes.visual: Grey salt squares appear crowded on the right of the membrane; one tries to cross and bounces off the dashed line. Small blue water dots appear on both sides. A question mark hangs over the membrane. No water movement is shown.
scenes.narration: But what if the crowded particle is one the membrane will not let through? And what if water is the only thing that can cross? That is the next film.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'Random moves make a one-way drift, no push needed.'
